indoorCorrection.title: Indoor Ride — Power Correction
indoorCorrection.indoorExplanation: Indoor rides produce less power at the same perceived effort due to heat accumulation and lack of air cooling. Your personal indoor/outdoor gap is used to scale TSS for accurate fitness tracking.
indoorCorrection.calibratePrompt: Complete at least 5 indoor and 5 outdoor rides with power data, then visit

chart.speedTip: Your speed over the ride in km/h. Consistent lines = steady pacing. Sharp dips = climbs or braking. A gradual drop in the second half may indicate fatigue.
chart.heartRateTip: Heart rate in BPM throughout the ride. A gradual rise is normal (cardiac drift). Spikes without speed change may indicate heat or fatigue. Aerobic base rides should stay in Z2: 60–70% of your max HR.
chart.cadenceTip: Pedal revolutions per minute (rpm). Optimal range is 75–90 rpm. High cadence (>90) means more cardiovascular load with less muscle fatigue. Low cadence (<70) stresses the muscles more and raises lactate.
chart.powerTip: Raw power output in watts. Spikes are normal for sprints and climbs. Sustained output above your FTP means threshold or harder effort. Compare with Normalized Power (NP) for the physiological cost of the whole ride.
chart.elevationTip: Altitude profile showing your terrain. Sharp spikes = steep climbs (or GPS noise). Total elevation gain is shown in the metrics above. Big climbs later in the ride are harder — check if your speed drops on them.

splits.title: Splits
splits.tip: Ride broken into equal distance chunks. Compare speed and HR across splits to spot pacing issues — if speed drops and HR rises in later splits, you went out too hard or are fatigued.

bestEfforts.title: Best Efforts
bestEfforts.tip: Fastest time for each target distance using a sliding window across the whole ride. These are your personal bests for this session — compare across rides to track fitness gains.

powerAnalysis.title: Power Analysis
powerAnalysis.tip: Advanced metrics from your power meter. NP (Normalized Power) is the physiological cost of the ride. IF (Intensity Factor) shows effort vs FTP. TSS is training load: <150 = overnight recovery, >300 = needs multiple easy days.
powerAnalysis.normPowerHint: Coggan NP — physiological cost of variable effort
powerAnalysis.cpDesc: CP = sustainable power indefinitely · W′ = anaerobic energy store depleted above CP. Fitted from 2–20 min MMP.
powerAnalysis.zonesBasedOnFtp: Power zones based on FTP of
powerAnalysis.mmpTitle: Mean Maximal Power (MMP) — best average power by duration
powerAnalysis.mmpSetFtp: · Set FTP in Settings to see zones

durability.title: Durability / Fatigue Resistance
durability.tip: Compares your power output fresh (first 40% of kJ) vs fatigued (remaining). <5% drop = excellent — you hold power well when tired. Pros typically drop <10%, amateurs 15–25%. Score = 100 − (avg drop% × 4).
durability.avgDrop: Avg drop: {{pct}}% · <5% pro level · 15–25% typical amateur · score = 100 − (drop% × 4)

powerQuadrant.title: Power Quadrant Analysis
powerQuadrant.tip: Breaks riding time into 4 quadrants by cadence and torque. Aerobic Spin (high cad, low torque) = efficient pedaling. Strength (low cad, high torque) = climbing. Sprint Power = short max efforts. More time in Aerobic Spin = better cycling economy.
powerQuadrant.cadenceSplit: Cadence split: {{rpm}} rpm · Torque split: {{nm}} Nm (median)

powerAnalysis.noFtpNudge: Set your FTP in Settings → Fitness Profile to unlock power zones, TSS, and intensity factor.

aerobicMetrics.title: Aerobic Metrics
aerobicMetrics.tipAdj: Adjusted Decoupling measures genuine aerobic drift by looking only at flat terrain segments and subtracting expected drift from heat and dehydration. <5% = good aerobic efficiency. The raw value is what the numbers show before corrections.
aerobicMetrics.tipRaw: HR Decoupling: how much your heart rate drifts up relative to pace across the ride. Below 5% = good aerobic base. Above 5% = fatigue, heat, or went too hard. VAM: your average climbing speed in m/h — 800 = solid endurance, 1500+ = pro climber.
aerobicMetrics.vamDesc: Climbing rate on ascending segments · 800 endurance · 1500+ pro climber

hrZones.title: Heart Rate Zones
hrZones.tip: Time in each HR zone based on your max HR. Z1–Z2 (60–70%) = aerobic base. Z3 (70–80%) = tempo. Z4–Z5 (80–100%) = high intensity. For endurance improvement, aim for 80%+ of your training time in Z1–Z2.
hrZones.basedOnMaxHr: Based on max HR of {{bpm}} bpm

cadenceZones.title: Cadence Zones
cadenceZones.tip: Distribution of cadence across the ride. Optimal zone (75–90 rpm) = efficient pedaling with balanced cardiovascular and muscular load. Most time here = good technique. More time in Very Low (<60 rpm) suggests you may be grinding gears.

hydration.title: Hydration & Heat Analysis
hydration.tip: Estimates your sweat loss and fluid needs based on ride sensor data, conditions, and intensity. Log your intake to see your deficit and personalised recommendations.
hydration.sourceTempWind: → {{eff}}°C effective (−{{cooling}}°C wind cooling from outdoor airflow)
hydration.sourceWindValue: {{speed}} km/h + ~20 km/h self-generated from cycling speed
hydration.sourceSweatCalibrated: Personal calibration ({{rate}} ml/h) — from your sweat test, scaled by conditions above 20°C / 55% RH
hydration.sourceSweatPopulation: Population average ({{rate}} ml/h) — add a sweat test in Settings for a personalised rate
hydration.sourceReferenceValue: Generic model would estimate ~{{rate}} ml/h for these conditions.
hydration.sourceReferenceLargeGap: Large gap vs generic model — if this feels wrong, check your sweat-test inputs in Settings.
hydration.noSweatTestNote: — run a sweat test for High confidence

dashboard.title: Dashboard
dashboard.emptyDesc: Upload your first .gpx or .fit file to get started
dashboard.trainingStatusTip: Fitness (CTL) = 42-day rolling training load. Fatigue (ATL) = 7-day load. Form (TSB) = Fitness − Fatigue. Positive form = fresh and ready. Negative = carrying training fatigue.
dashboard.uploadToTrack: Upload a few rides to start tracking fitness.
dashboard.weeklyLoadTip: Green bars = distance per week (this week highlighted). Red line = training stress (TSS) — how hard those kilometres were. Aim for gradual increases with a lighter recovery week every 3–4 weeks.
dashboard.durabilityTip: How well you hold your aerobic efficiency late into a ride (0–100). Higher = less fade in the final hour. Long steady rides build it.
dashboard.heatReadinessTip: How adapted you are to riding in the heat, based on hot rides in the last 14 days. Your sweat rate sets personal hydration targets on ride pages.

form_status.veryFreshDesc: Fully recovered — ideal for a big effort, but fitness fades if you coast here too long.
form_status.freshDesc: Recovered and ready. Good day to go hard.
form_status.balancedDesc: Normal training balance. Keep riding as planned.
form_status.buildingDesc: Carrying fatigue — productive overload, but keep an eye on recovery.
form_status.overreachingDesc: Heavy fatigue. An easy spin or rest day will help more than another hard ride.
